2027-01-07.title: Thursday after Denho · The Praise of St John the Baptist
readings: A servant of the gospel by the gift of God's grace
Among those born of women no one is greater than John
2027-01-07.verse: I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.
theo: On the day after Denho the Syriac tradition praises the one who baptised the Lord. Jesus himself gives John's praise: “What did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind?” No, John was firm. “Someone dressed in soft robes?” No, he lived in poverty. “A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.” He is the messenger foretold to prepare the way. “Among those born of women no one is greater than John.”

And then a surprise: “yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he.” John stood at the threshold; we, by Baptism, have entered. The grace of the Kingdom is greater than any human greatness. Paul calls himself “the very least of all the saints”, yet a servant of the Gospel “according to the gift of God's grace”. The mystery hidden for ages is now revealed: the Gentiles are fellow heirs in Christ. John prepared the way; we are sent to walk it.

illus: A coconut palm on a Kerala beach bends in every storm but its roots go deep, and it does not fall. A reed by the canal is flattened by the first gust. John the Baptist was a palm rooted in God.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you praised John the Baptist as more than a prophet. Make us firm like him, and grateful for the grace of your Kingdom. Amen.
share: A reed shaken by the wind? (Luke 7:24). What winds shake my faith?
More than a prophet (Luke 7:26). Who prepared the way of Jesus in my life?
The least in the kingdom is greater than he (Luke 7:28). How do I value the grace of my Baptism?
pm.resp: Lord, make us firm in faith.
interc: For the Church, that she may prepare the way of the Lord in our time.
For prophets and preachers, that they may be firm and simple.
For those shaken by doubt or fear.
For our group, that we may walk the way John prepared.
pm.close: Father, you sent John to prepare the way of your Son. Make us firm in faith and grateful for the grace of the Kingdom. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, on the day after Denho the Syriac Churches praise John the Baptist, who baptised the Lord in the Jordan. Jesus himself speaks his praise.

He asks the crowds: what did you go out into the wilderness to look at? A reed shaken by the wind? (Luke 7:24). No. John was not shaken by public opinion or by Herod's power. Someone dressed in soft robes? No. John lived in poverty.
A prophet? Yes, says Jesus, and more than a prophet. He is the messenger sent ahead to prepare the way. Among those born of women no one is greater than John (Luke 7:28).

Then a surprise: yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he. John stood at the door; by Baptism we have entered. This is not about our merit but about grace. Paul calls himself a servant of the gospel according to the gift of God's grace (Ephesians 3:7).
Let us honour John by being firm in faith, simple in life, and grateful for the Kingdom we have received. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said John the Baptist was very great and strong, like a tree in a storm. Let us be strong for Jesus too!
